newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply lower on Brazil news.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply lower on Brazil news.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended sharply lower amid news a U.S. firm purchased 45,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans for import into the United States, traders said.
"Brazil is on stream now, not just to Europe and the Pacific Rim but to us, too," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

Glencore Brazil said it sold 45,000 tonnes of soybeans to a U.S. firm, most likely for April or May shipment. U.S. exporters said the deal made economic sense because Brazilian soybeans were better quality and cheaper than U.S. supplies.

Floor sources said the soybeans were likely destined for a crushing plant along the Ohio River and the soymeal would then be shipped to southeast poultry feedlots. Other sources suggested the buyer was in Georgia.

Traders said the sale may have ended a two-month soy complex rally because it proved U.S. supplies were no longer competitive. While the market knew Brazil had ample soybean supplies, it hadn't expected them to come to the U.S.
Soymeal ended down $9.60 to $2.30 per ton with May off $7.80 at $266.00 a ton. Soyoil closed down 0.83 to 0.75 cent per lb with May down 0.83 at 25.34 cents per lb.

The news came just as the Philippines was considering buying South American soymeal instead of U.S. supplies. The Philippines planned to import 1.4 million tonnes of soymeal this year, up from 1.2 million last year.
Floor sources also cited speculation that eastern Corn Belt farmers would replant flood-damaged acreage to soybeans, especially with new crop soybean values at a lofty $7.35-1/2 per bushel.
Rains in the U.S. South were delaying rice sowings, and traders suggested soybeans would also draw some acres away from rice.

But reports that several major U.S. crushers were taking downtime this month were seen as supportive and crushing rates were expected to drop this week. Cargill Inc's Guntersville crusher will be down for about two weeks, a Cargill official said.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 500 lots May soymeal and 100 lots July while Continental Grain bought 300 May and 100 March, traders said.
Produce Grain sold 400 lots July soymeal, 200 May and 100 each March and August. E.D. and F. Man International sold 500 lots May and Rosenthal Collins sold 600 May.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 1,600 lots May while Produce Grain sold 500 May and 200 July, traders said.
Refco Inc sold 800 lots May and O'Connor and Co sold 300 May.
